Assets.ReleaseNotes:
Version 0.1.70

What changed:
- Outlook Classic and other legacy text targets no longer report success just because Windows accepted a paste command.
- If legacy paste cannot be verified, PassiFlow now leaves the final text on the clipboard and reports the insertion as unverified instead of risking duplicate text.
- Outlook/Office targets now try direct text insertion before legacy clipboard paste, so old false-success preferences are avoided.

Version 0.1.69

What changed:
- Outlook Classic and other legacy Office/Win32 editors now have an extra paste fallback when normal Ctrl+V insertion fails.
- PassiFlow now learns the insertion method that works per app, so future dictations can prefer the successful path automatically.
- Prompt preset labels and text-field spacing were polished.
- Vocabulary and text macro editors now use a clearer, wider layout.
- Custom vocabulary is included in cleanup prompts again, so dictated terms can be corrected more reliably.

Version 0.1.52

What changed:
- Harden PassiFlow cleanup and recording flow.
- Show model rate limit usage hints.
- Bound PassiFlow transcribing stalls.
- Suppress temporary clipboard history.
- Delay clipboard restore after paste.
- Stabilize PassiFlow paste and release validation.

Version 0.1.51

What changed:
- Model dropdowns can now show compact provider usage hints such as remaining tokens and reset time when PassiFlow receives rate-limit headers.
- Dictation is less likely to stay stuck in Transcribing because post-processing requests now use bounded timeouts and safer UI/history dispatch.
- Temporary transcript clipboard writes are excluded from Windows clipboard history and cloud sync when possible.
- Clipboard paste restore timing was tuned for browser, Electron, and terminal targets, reducing post-dictation delay while keeping insertion reliable.
- Run Log retry/status handling is more reliable after retrying failed transcriptions.
